title: Reachability simulation by the tape machine
statement: Fix a Boolean input $x$, an arithmetic register program $A$, its initial state $l_0$, an oracle, a multi-tape machine $D$, a choice of initial state for $D$ for each oracle index, and bounds $B,W\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose an $N$-step register computation from state $l$ and valuation $v$, with no answer yet, ends in state $l'$, valuation $v'$, and no answer. Assume that at every earlier step its configuration satisfies the register-program precondition for $D$ and the chosen oracle, and each register value plus one has binary length at most $W$. Then the tape machine compiled from $A$ can run from the initial tape configuration encoding $x,l,v$ and the given output word to the corresponding configuration encoding $x,l',v'$ with that output word unchanged, while its invariant holds at every earlier step.
hypotheses_covered: Oracle, multi-tape machine $D$, and oracle-indexed initial states for $D$
Register computation has $N$ steps and exact stated endpoint
At each time less than $N$, the precondition for the program, machine, and oracle holds
At each time less than $N$, every register value plus one has binary length at most $W
